newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS - First Austrian still in Creditanstalt race.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - First Austrian still in Creditanstalt race.

text.p: First Austrian bank reinforced its determination to win a stake in privatisation candidate Creditanstalt-Bankverein on Friday and said a cooperation could be beneficial to both institutions.

Die Erste Oesterreichische SparCasse Bank AG (First Austrian) has argued that an alliance with Creditanstalt through a holding company would end the government's six-year struggle to sell the nation's number two bank and go some way to cleaning up the overcrowded financial sector.
"The aim of such a cooperation would be that both banks would profit from it," First Austrian chief executive Konrad Fuchs said at an investment fair.
His comments came hours after news of yet another setback in Creditanstalt's marathon privatisation.

Sources close to the bank said the finance ministry had postponed a fresh call for bids until the end of next week at the earliest. Finance Minister Viktor Klima had planned to restart the ill-fated sale this week.
"It really is a never-ending story," said an international analyst.
"I am extremely keen to see this matter cleared up," said Creditanstalt's weary chief executive, Guido Schmidt-Chiari.
He has seen a host of suitors come and go since the Austrian government first put Creditanstalt at the top of its privatisation list in 1990.

The most recent bid, from an international consortium headed by insurer EA-Generali, foundered last month because the group was reluctant to take on all of the state's 19.9 million shares, representing 70 percent of ordinary voting stock.
Then the finance ministry said it had asked U.S. investment house J.P. Morgan to update a study of the bank by October 11. A four to six-week bidding period would follow.
At current market prices the government's shares are worth almost 14 billion schillings ($1.3 billion) -- well below the 18 billion schillings the finance ministry had been targeting.
Fuchs declined to comment on whether First Austrian, one of Austria's top five banks, would consider rejoining the EA-Generali consortium.
First Austrian quit the group, which also includes Germany's Commerzbank and Italy's Banca Commerciale Italiana, in September and swiftly announced plans to set up a rival bid.
But last week EA-Generali said the two sides were back in talks to overcome their differences.
"We are very interested to see an accord with First Austrian. We would welcome their return," EA-Generali chief executive Dietrich Karner said.
Fuchs merely responded that Austrian and foreign firms had already shown a keen interest in joining a First Austrian bid.

Creditanstalt ordinary shares closed 3.9 schillings up at 689 on Friday. "The share price looks good, but it would be even better with a (First Austrian-Creditanstalt) cooperation," Fuchs said. ($1=10.75 Schilling)
